Simulate iBOIN Trials

Source: R/iboin_simulate.R
iboin_simulate.Rd

Run the iBOIN dose-finding algorithm of Zhou et al. (2021) over many simulated trials and return the patient and DLT counts at every dose. This is the simulation engine behind sim_iboin, exposed for users who want the raw trial data.

Usage

iboin_simulate(
  target,
  p_true,
  skeleton,
  prior_ess,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  n_trials = 10000,
  start_dose = 1,
  n_earlystop = 18,
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  extrasafe = FALSE,
  offset = 0.05,
  robust = FALSE,
  n_earlystop_rule = c("with_stay", "simple"),
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Target DLT probability, for example 0.30.

p_true

Numeric vector. True DLT probability at each dose level, in increasing dose order.

skeleton

Numeric vector, one value per dose. Prior DLT probability at each dose, strictly between 0 and 1.

prior_ess

Whole number or vector of whole numbers, one per dose. Prior effective sample size. See iboin_boundary.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or vector. Number of patients per cohort. A scalar is used for every cohort. A vector shorter than n_cohort is padded with its last element and a longer one is truncated.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

start_dose

Integer scalar. Dose level for the first cohort. Defaults to 1.

n_earlystop

Integer scalar. The trial stops once this many patients have been treated at the current dose and the design would stay there. Defaults to 18. The simulations of the article do not stop early; a value above the maximum sample size switches the rule off.

p_saf

Numeric scalar. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.6 * target.

p_tox

Numeric scalar. Lowest DLT probability deemed overly toxic. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. Posterior probability cutoff for dose elimination. Defaults to 0.95.

extrasafe

Logical scalar. Apply the stricter safety stopping rule at the lowest dose. Defaults to FALSE.

offset

Numeric scalar between 0 and 0.5. Amount by which cutoff_eli is relaxed for the safety stopping rule. Defaults to 0.05.

robust

Logical scalar. Use the robust prior, which drops the prior information above the prior MTD when the prior MTD lies in the upper half of the doses. Defaults to FALSE. See iboin_boundary.

n_earlystop_rule

Character scalar, either "with_stay" or "simple". Under "with_stay" the trial stops at n_earlystop only when the design would remain at the current dose. Under "simple" it stops as soon as the threshold is reached.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. When NULL the current state of the random number generator is used. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class c("iboin_trials", "boin_trials"), which is a list with components

n_pts

Integer matrix, n_trials by number of doses, of patients treated.

n_tox

Integer matrix of the same shape, of DLTs observed.

eliminated

Logical matrix of the same shape, marking doses eliminated during the trial.

cohorts_used

Integer vector of cohorts completed in each trial.

stop_reason

Character vector giving why each trial ended.

boundary

The iboin_boundary object used.

design

The name of the design, "iBOIN".

settings

List of the design parameters.

Details

The trial runs as a BOIN trial, see boin_simulate, with the boundaries of iboin_boundary, which depend on the dose and on the number of patients treated there. Dose elimination and the safety stopping rule use a uniform prior, as in the BOIN design. The titration of the BOIN design is not available.

One uniform variate is drawn per patient, in enrollment order, and a cohort cut short by the maximum sample size still draws a full cohort's worth. With a prior effective sample size of 0 at every dose the trials are therefore, for the same seed, those of boin_simulate.

Possible values of stop_reason are "lowest_dose_eliminated", "lowest_dose_too_toxic", "n_earlystop", "max_sample_size" and "max_cohorts".

References

Zhou, Y., Lee, J. J., Wang, S., Bailey, S. and Yuan, Y. (2021). Incorporating historical information to improve phase I clinical trials. Pharmaceutical Statistics, 20, 1017-1034. doi:10.1002/pst.2121

See also

sim_iboin, iboin_boundary, boin_select_mtd

Examples

trials <- iboin_simulate(
  target = 0.30,
  p_true = c(0.08, 0.15, 0.31, 0.45, 0.55),
  skeleton = c(0.10, 0.19, 0.30, 0.42, 0.54),
  prior_ess = 3,
  n_cohort = 10,
  cohort_size = 3,
  n_trials = 200,
  seed = 123
)
trials
#> Simulated iBOIN trials
#>   trials          : 200
#>   doses           : 5
#>   target DLT rate : 0.3
#>   cohorts         : 10 of size 3
#>   max sample size : 30
#> 
#> Average per trial:
#>                   DL1  DL2   DL3  DL4  DL5
#> Patients treated 3.52 8.84 12.63 3.86 0.42
#> DLTs observed    0.31 1.30  3.86 1.81 0.22
#> 
#> Stopping reason (%):
#> 
#> max_sample_size     n_earlystop 
#>              82              18 

head(trials$n_pts)
#>      DL1 DL2 DL3 DL4 DL5
#> [1,]   3   6   9   9   3
#> [2,]   3  18   6   0   0
#> [3,]   3   6  15   6   0
#> [4,]   3   6   9   6   6
#> [5,]   3  18   6   0   0
#> [6,]   3  15  12   0   0
table(trials$stop_reason)
#> 
#> max_sample_size     n_earlystop 
#>             164              36
